study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting Heterogeneity in Functional Network Connectivity Aberrations in Antipsychotic Medication-Naïve First Episode Psychosis Patients - A Normative Modeling Study

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are explicitly stated in the Abstract, and the purpose of applying normative modeling is to characterize individual-level deviations and assess whether normative values can identify biologically less heterogeneous subgroups.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Objective: To characterize inter-individual heterogeneity in functional networks and investigate if normative values can be leveraged to identify biologically less heterogeneous subgroups of patients. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Individual-level patterns of deviations from a normative reference range in resting-state functional networks.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study uses an EXISTING normative model. The original normative reference work is cited in the Introduction (reference to normative reference curves for large-scale resting-state networks) and the PCN toolkit is named with version. Local calibration with healthy controls is described, including detailed eligibility criteria for the local reference sample. Image quality and data completeness standards are specified (motion/outlier criteria). Final sample sizes are reported (HC N=122; patients N=108). However, the source datasets composing the ~22,000 healthy individuals are not named and reasons for exclusion are not enumerated.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Here, we used the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience (PCN) toolkit (version 0.27)... cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are defined as z-scores relative to the normative range, with explicit thresholds (|Z| ≥ 2) used to define significant deviations. The direction (positive/increased; negative/decreased connectivity) is specified, and clinical relevance is discussed via subgrouping to identify biologically less heterogeneous patient clusters.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: We quantified functional connection deviations expressed as standard deviations (z-score) from the normative reference range... We binarized z-scores... using a cut-off value of ±2 standard deviations... We grouped individuals according to plausible functional deviation profiles: (1) only positive deviations (increased connectivity), (2) only negative deviations (decreased connectivity), (3) mix... (4) none... We discovered that all four subgroups do exist... and showed that subgroups based on deviation profiles were significantly less heterogeneous...
